As of 310 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Rain chances and gusty winds look to linger 
along the coast Friday depending on the track of the developing 
nor'easter.   

Latest sfc analysis shows low pressure continuing to develop 
offshore just to the southeast of the local area. Cool, cloudy, and 
gusty conditions have persisted today as well as light misty showers 
along the coast. Wind Advisories are still in effect through this 
evening for coastal zones including Norfolk and Portsmouth for gusts 
of 35 to 45mph. Dangerous surf, beach erosion, and moderate to major 
tidal flooding will continue for the next few days. Please see the 
sections below for further details.

Overnight through tomorrow, low pressure starts to slide north and 
high pressure tries to build in from the northwest. Expecting some 
clearing of cloud cover over the piedmont by the morning and 
remaining partly cloudy through the day tomorrow. Meanwhile at the 
coast, thick cloud cover and intermittent drizzle will persist on 
the backside of that low. Temps tonight drop as low as the upper 40s 
in western counties and low to mid 50s elsewhere. Cooler temps 
continue tomorrow, though perhaps a touch warmer where the sun can 
peek through with highs approaching 70. 

Uncertainty increases Friday night into Saturday regarding the track 
of the nor'easter. The 12z global ensembles and the high res models 
are in pretty good agreement that the system will curve west into 
the coast, but there is disagreement on how far south that would 
happen. Some models take the center low up to New York and southern 
New England while the more southern solutions take it into New 
Jersey. The latter would result in higher winds and lingering 
clouds/drizzle into Saturday, especially on the Eastern Shore. 
Currently forecasting wind gusts of 20 to 30mph (highest along the 
coast) for Saturday, but may need to increase it on the Eastern 
Shore if the more southern solution persists in the models. 
Otherwise, expecting warmer temperatures Saturday inland with highs 
in the mid to upper 70s while the cooler temps in the 60s persist on 
the Eastern Shore. Similar temps and relatively lighter winds 
expected Sunday. 

High pressure builds into the region late Monday through Wednesday 
giving us a break with dry weather and sunshine. Temperatures will 
be able to warm more each day with the ridging overhead. On Monday, 
expect low to mid 70s for the north and upper 70s to near 80 degrees 
across the south. By mid-week, we may be well above normal once 
again (mid 80s) as southerly flow develops ahead of the next cold 
front. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Widespread moderate to locally major tidal flooding 
(inundation of 2-3 feet AGL in vulnerable areas) will continue 
through tomorrow night at most spots, with some locations especially 
in the middle Bay potentially seeing moderate coastal flooding 
through Saturday or Sunday.

As low pressure develops off the coast, winds have backed slightly 
today over the region, now closer to North-Northeast instead of NE. 
In addition, the speeds have also decreased slightly at 20-30 kt 
with gusts to 35 kt. However, this has done little to change the 
coastal flood situation with most sites currently seeing anomalies 
of 2.5-3.5 ft above normal astronomical tide today. With little 
change overnight into Friday, expect similar anomalies tonight and 
even into Friday. These anomalies combined with higher astronomical 
tides through tomorrow will likely keep similar flooding as has been 
experienced for the last few high tide cycles. As such, have opted 
to extend the coastal flood warning for all sites through Friday 
night. 

Overall, storm surge guidance has trended higher with the 12z runs 
inside the bay Saturday and even Sunday. This is likely due to the 
models depicting the offshore low pressure potentially being 
slightly stronger and further west than previous runs. While this 
will lead to a more N-NW flow inside the bay leading to more ebbing 
at the mouth of the Bay, it is also possible that especially the 
eastern side of the Bay could see increased water levels with a 
better onshore component to the winds. As such, have opted to 
increase the tides slightly into Saturday for the middle Bay and 
eastern side of the bay. There is still uncertainty in the tide 
forecast for the weekend, so we will not extend the warnings into 
the weekend at this time but it is quite possible that some warnings 
will need to be extended.
